_comment: Descriptive connector manifest for humans/registration tooling — not a normative MCP protocol file. The live, authoritative tool schemas are served at runtime by mcp_server/server.py itself (FastMCP introspects the @mcp_app.tool()-decorated function signatures/docstrings).
name: transbench
description: TransBench -- a translational clinician<->bench research agent. Decomposes ANY clinical/biomedical observation (any disease, drug, or mechanism -- the PubMed anchor is derived per-observation, not fixed to one domain) into biological axes, generates up to 3 falsifiable mechanistic hypotheses, grounds each in retrieved PubMed evidence (support + contradiction), applies a novelty guard (established/open_question/unsupported) so textbook facts are never shipped as novel, and designs ONE reproducible computational experiment naming a concrete, resolvable public dataset plus a claude_science_prompt. Research tool only -- never diagnosis, drug selection, or dosing advice; every response carries a fixed disclaimer.

stdio.note: the transport Claude Science spawns per CLAUDE_SCIENCE_SETUP.md Step 4

http.note: demo-day fallback only (CLAUDE_SCIENCE_SETUP.md); also try sdk_transport=sse if a client only speaks the older SSE transport -- both are supported by mcp==1.28.1

required.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: BYOK key for the ENGINE's own Anthropic calls (create_llm user_key) -- independent of Claude Science, which is only this tool's MCP client.

tools.name: generate_experiment
tools.summary: The showpiece. Full grounded TransBrief incl. one runnable computational experiment. ASYNC (submit + poll): starts a background job and returns a job_id in <1s; the full brief is fetched via get_experiment_result. This is because a run legitimately takes ~60-120s (longer cold), beyond an MCP client's single-call wait-for-result timeout.
tools.returns: Immediately {job_id, status:'running', poll_tool:'get_experiment_result', message}; then poll get_experiment_result(job_id) -> {status:'done', result:<TransBrief, see src/transbench/schemas.py>} or {status:'error', result:{error, message, status_code}}. Obviously-invalid input is rejected inline as {error, message, status_code} (no job).
tools.cost_note: ~13 LLM calls + live PubMed + live GEO verification per invocation (BUILD_SPEC.md §9)

tools.name: search_grounded_evidence
tools.summary: Utility/fallback. Same engine run as generate_experiment, reshaped into a lighter grounded-evidence projection (no axes/top_experiment/run_manifest). ASYNC (submit + poll), same as generate_experiment.
tools.returns: Immediately {job_id, status:'running', poll_tool:'get_experiment_result', message}; then poll get_experiment_result(job_id) -> {status:'done', result:{request_echo, hypotheses[{...,evidence[]}], references[], contradictions_surfaced[], uncertainty_note, disclaimer}} or {status:'error', result:{error, message, status_code}}.
tools.cost_note: same cost as generate_experiment -- it is the same full pipeline, only the RETURNED shape is lighter

tools.name: get_experiment_result
tools.summary: Poll for the outcome of a generate_experiment / search_grounded_evidence job. Fast (<1s) every call, so no single call ever nears the client's wait-for-result timeout however long the run takes.
tools.returns: {status:'running', job_id} while working; {status:'done', job_id, result:<brief or projection>} when complete; {status:'error', job_id, result:{error, message, status_code}} on failure; {error:'unknown_job', message, status_code:404} for an unknown/expired job_id (finished results retained ~MCP_JOB_TTL_SECONDS, default 1800s).
tools.cost_note: free -- pure registry lookup, no engine/LLM/PubMed calls

disclaimer: Research hypothesis generation only. Not clinical, diagnostic, or prescribing advice.
